memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "But the Lord will make a distinction between the livestock of Israel and that of Egypt, so that no animal belonging to the Israelites will die.'" The Lord set a time and said, "Tomorrow the Lord will do this in the land."" - Exodus 9:4-5 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Again God draws the line at Goshen. Not one animal belonging to Israel will die.

This is not because Israel was better. It is because they belonged to God, and He knew exactly which animals in which fields were theirs. The precision is astonishing. God's care operates at the level of individual livestock in a foreign country.

If God tracks cattle that carefully, consider what Jesus said about His Father knowing when a single sparrow falls, and even numbering the hairs of our heads (Mt 10:29-31).

We must be careful, though, not to twist this into a promise that believers will never lose anything. Job lost all his livestock. Christians lose homes, health and loved ones. The distinction Scripture guarantees is not exemption from loss but belonging that loss cannot break.

Notice also the last line: the Lord set a time. God is not improvising. He announces the hour in advance so that no one can call it coincidence.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I really believe God's care extends to the small details of my life?
2. Am I trusting God for protection, or trusting Him because I belong to Him?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You know exactly what is Yours, including me. Help me to rest in belonging to You. Amen.
